In general, drinking a lot of clean water is going to help keep your body healthy. If at all possible, give up all fluids besides water. Your kidneys are basically just water filters for the digestive system, and we all know that dirty fluids clog a filter faster that clean water. Drinking lots of water can also help dislodge existing stones that might be causing pain. If your urine is more than slightly yellow, more water is needed (unless you take B vitamins supplements, in which case your pee will be yellow no matter what). Often chronic kidney issues are related to diabetes or high blood pressure. As you probably know, type II diabetes is caused by a diet extremely high in sugars. High blood pressure is generally a symptom of being overweight, which also comes back to eating too much sugar. Salt is another big factor with blood pressure.

As far as diet goes, most of the bases are covered by the ketogenic diet. Keep the salt intake low, and choose meats that do not have added phosphorus. Also make sure you're getting proper potassium.

Funny thing though, in the 1st world we get most of our iodine through enriched table salt. This means that some people who eat a ton of salt can actually get iodine toxicity. A blood test is the only way to know for sure, but people with chronic kidney disease usually have a harder time processing even normal amounts of iodine. The feedback loop between iodine/salt/blood pressure is a great example of how we can get stuck being unhealthy, even if most of our diet is in check.

And finally on the kidney topic: drugs. There's a short list of medications that are thought to cause stones.
